scenes.heading: Ratio, rates and speed
scenes.say: Sharing money, comparing prices, timing a journey — ratio, rate and speed questions all compare amounts by multiplying and dividing. Let's see the methods that make them quick.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Sharing a chocolate bar cut into equal squares
scenes.science: A ratio 3 : 5 means 8 equal parts; find one part first
scenes.breaks: chocolate squares are physical; ratio parts can be any size, even fractions.
scenes.say: Think of a chocolate bar cut into equal squares. A ratio of three to five means eight equal squares, three for one person and five for the other. Find the size of one square first, then everything else follows.

scenes.heading: Share in a ratio
scenes.question: Share $72 in the ratio 3 : 5.
scenes.say: Share seventy-two dollars in the ratio three to five. There are eight parts, so one part is nine dollars. That gives twenty-seven dollars and forty-five dollars, which add back to seventy-two.
scenes.caption: Share $72 in the ratio 3 : 5. There are 8 parts, so one part is $9. That gives $27 and $45, which add to $72.

scenes.heading: Speed, distance, time
scenes.say: Speed equals distance divided by time. If speed is in kilometres per hour, change minutes into hours first. Thirty minutes is half an hour.

scenes.heading: Average speed trap
scenes.say: Drive sixty kilometres at sixty, then back at thirty. Don't average the speeds to get forty-five. You spend longer going slowly. Total distance, one hundred and twenty, divided by total time, three hours, gives forty kilometres per hour.

scenes.heading: Working together
points: Write the job done in 1 hour
Flip to get the total time
scenes.say: For working together, write how much of the job each does in one hour, add them, then flip the answer. Together is always faster than either one alone.
Quick recap. For ratios, find one part first. Use unit rates for best buys, change minutes into hours, and use total over total for average speed. Now try the practice questions!
